channel.title: EU & Swiss News Feed
channel.description: Latest news from Europe covering politics, economy, and security

item.title: [EU Observer] What kind of ECB is Europe getting after Lagarde?
item.description: Now that Paris and Berlin appear to have lined up Spanish central banker Pablo Hernández de Cos for the ECB presidency instead of his Dutch counterpart Klaas Knot, whether a dove or a hawk sits at the top may matter less than it seems, including for France.

item.title: [DW] Hashim Thaci's second conviction in The Hague reignites debate in Kosovo about justice and the Kosovo Specialist Chambers
item.description: Former President Hashim Thaci has been convicted of trying to influence witnesses in his war crimes trial. The conviction has reignited debate in Kosovo about the Kosovo Specialist Chambers, the court that convicted him.

item.title: [DW] Back to 1997: Russia wants NATO to roll back its eastern expansion
item.description: The Kremlin is reportedly calling on NATO to withdraw from large parts of Eastern Europe. What this would mean for the security of millions of Europeans — and what lies behind Russia's plan.

item.title: [DW] Rights court rules Turkey must release jailed lawmaker Atalay
item.description: The European Court of Human Rights has called for the release of imprisoned elected lawmaker Can Atalay. Atalay has been in prison for almost five years despite rulings from the Turkish Constitutional Court.

item.title: [DW] Students' List candidates take seats as Serbian parliament opens
item.description: Serbia's Student List's candidates have taken their oaths in the inaugural parliament session. As the new majority, they have 90 days to form a government.

item.title: [DW] 'Humanitarian mission' for Kostiantynivka: Is it a trap?
item.description: Russian President Putin has proposed an evacuation of the Ukrainian city of Kostiantynivka, like the recent operation in Oleshky. Experts warn this could serve military, not humanitarian, aims. What should Kyiv do?

item.title: [EU Observer] Italy’s hard definition of antisemitism will shield Israeli crimes and harm free speech
item.description: Italy's Meloni has doubled down on her populist and performative claims to care about Jewish minorities, by imposing a hardline definition of antisemitism that risks gagging debate.

item.title: [EU Observer] UK-EU summit to see mutual love-bombing, but British must decide what to do next
item.description: There will be agreements aplenty in Brussels on Friday, but the UK needs to decide how ambitious its plans for closer integration with the EU will be.

item.title: [EU Observer] Hungary’s new government claws back motorways and tobacco monopoly after years of taxpayer‑funded Orbán luxury travel (Day 191 of the Tisza government)
item.description: Hungary’s new leaders rip up motorway and tobacco deals that once enriched Orbán’s allies, raising the prospect of a massive financial and political reckoning.

item.title: [EU Observer] Ukrainians hit Crimea’s railway bridge with Neptune missiles, but it is harder to destroy than the road bridge (Ukraine Battlefield update, Day 1,729)
item.description: Ukraine’s strikes on the Crimean railway bridge and Russia’s refineries are no longer just symbolic blows, but a coordinated effort to choke off fuel, supplies, and troop movements deep inside Russian-held territory.

item.title: [EU Observer] EU gives oil and gas importers until 2029 on methane checks, rules out more delay
item.description: After all-night talks, EU governments and MEPs agreed to delay methane regulations until 2029, but scrapped the legal possibility for further fob-offs, in a win for centre-left politics.

item.title: [DW] EU Commission confirms it was targeted in cyberattack using AI tools
item.description: The European Commission was targeted by an "AI-generated cybercampaign," a spokesperson has said. This is the first time the bloc has publicly reported an AI-based cyberattack.

item.title: [EU Observer] MEPs gut EU Commission plan for regulating space industries
item.description: Brussels is racing to keep up in the global space race, after MEPs slashed green demands from the EU’s first Space Act, in a bid to win over capitals and industry.

item.title: [DW] Wadephul: 'Coalition of the Willing' talks in Berlin send strong signal to Moscow
item.description: German Foreign Minister Wadephul has said the Coalition of the Willing meeting in Berlin sends a clear message to Moscow to take peace talks seriously. He also warned Ukraine should be prepared for peace talks to fail.

item.title: [EU Observer] Erdoğan is strangling Turkey’s last free media, as EU turns a blind eye
item.description: Turkey's state takeover of independent broadcaster Sözcü TV was met by loud EU silence, in a broader pattern of appeasement, as Erdoğan strangles what is left of free speech.

item.title: [EU Observer] Listen: Is the EU’s Digital Services Act actually working?
item.description: Earlier this week, the European Commission stepped up its action against Chinese online marketplace Temu. It announced that the platform was once again in breach of the Digital Services Act (DSA), and could face further fines.

item.title: [EU Observer] The same EU Parliament that built the Ethics Body is now killing it, in violation of European law
item.description: Two and a half years after signing the agreement, the EU Parliament is blocking its own ethics body before it has met even once, but EU law does not allow it to walk away so easily, and nor should parliament president Metsola.

item.title: [EU Observer] EU should tax Big Tech and crypto to help farmers in next budget, Spanish socialist MEP says
item.description: As EU leaders wrangle over Europe’s next long-term budget, socialist MEP Sandra Gómez López warns that unless Big Tech, online gambling, and crypto start paying more, farmers and poorer regions will be the ones footing the bill.

item.title: [DW] EU leaders tussle over whom to send to Ukraine, Russia peace talks
item.description: A seat at the table for Europe now appears likely following comments by a US envoy who just held talks with Putin. But who will take that seat remains unclear.

item.title: [DW] Despite restrictive abortion laws, Poland's 'Abortomat' — a locker that dispenses abortion pills — helps women who want to end a pregnancy
item.description: Abortion laws in Poland are very restrictive. Activists there have found a new way to help women wanting to terminate a pregnancy: the "Abortomat," a locker that dispenses abortion pills. But they face fierce opposition.

item.title: [DW] Ukraine: Zelenskyy says security deal could go to referendum
item.description: The US has broached the idea of Kyiv giving up the Donbas region in exchange for NATO membership, the Ukrainian president said.

item.title: [DW] Turkey uses espionage accusations to pressure government critics
item.description: The arrest of a German foundation's employee in Istanbul this week has put the focus back on pressure tactics used by the Erdogan administration. The arrest is far from the first of its kind.

item.title: [DW] Gen Z protests: Do Baby Boomers really have it better than young people?
item.description: Should young people in Germany be more worried about their future than Baby Boomers were in the 1980s and 1990s? Or should both generations take to the streets and protest together? DW checked the data.

item.description: Domestic political considerations had reportedly contributed to the delay

item.title: [Financial Times] How Anthropic’s blockbuster IPO came together
item.description: Fears about the AI trade did not damp enthusiasm for shares. But can the low-key company preserve its idiosyncratic culture in the glare of public markets?

item.title: [Politico Europe] German defense minister apologizes for calling US criticism of Ukraine strikes ‘stupid’
item.description: Boris Pistorius walked back his choice of words but stood by his support for Ukrainian strikes inside Russia.

item.title: [Politico Europe] Marine Le Pen’s party faces scrutiny over alleged leaks from interior ministry
item.description: A senior civil servant is under investigation for reportedly passing on confidential judicial information to the National Rally.

item.title: [Euractiv] EU warns COP31 could fail without commitment on fossil fuels
item.description: “It won’t fly,” an EU official told Rapporteur of the latest draft agreement

item.title: [Politico Europe] Some oil giants will now be labeled ‘sustainable’ under EU finance rules
item.description: The agreement came the same day the EU agreed to delay methane emission rules for fossil fuel companies.

item.title: [DW] EU and UK hold a rare summit in bid to 'rebuild ties'
item.description: European Union officials and UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham met in Brussels to discuss efforts to rebuild ties following Brexit.

item.description: Europe's negotiators won’t let UN climate talks close with attack on CBAM, parliamentary negotiator Mohammed Chahim says

item.title: [Financial Times] UK and EU agree Brexit ‘reset’ but delivery rests on tuition fees
item.description: Brussels insists Britain must cut university fees for bloc’s students

item.description: The southern region is home to Airbus and an air and space industry cluster

item.description: Spain's leftist leaders have accuse the ruling Socialists of stealing their electoral programmes

item.title: [EU Observer] ‘He who pays the piper calls the tune’: Czech media-freedom attack is part of wider EU malaise, ex-commissioner Věra Jourová says
item.description: Věra Jourová, former values commissioner and vice-president of the EU Commission, warns of the consequences of abolishing licence fees in the Czech Republic, while warning of numerous attacks on media freedom across Europe.

item.title: [Politico Europe] ‘Staff deserve answers’ on Commission cyberattack, union says
item.description: EU executive “yet to send a single update to all staff" about recent cyberattack, union email says.

item.title: [Politico Europe] Brussels to link UK-EU summit package to tuition fee demands
item.description: Brussels denies it is taking Britain "hostage" despite insisting student fees are part of wider “package.”

item.title: [Politico Europe] Germany says investors ready to spend €25B to buy TikTok Europe
item.description: Germany and Austria floated the initiative earlier this week, citing concerns about the Chinese-owned company's influence on European democracy.

item.title: [Politico Europe] Emmanuel Macron hosts Kamala Harris at Elysée
item.description: The French leader is hosting the former vice president in a "private capacity," the Elysée said.

item.title: [Politico Europe] Russia hits 3 Kyiv bridges in major attack, while Poland reports airspace violation
item.description: The overnight strikes, which killed at least five people across Ukraine, came hours after Vladimir Putin vowed a painful response to Ukraine’s attacks on the Crimean bridge.

item.description: In today's edition: Ukraine exercise, Lithuanian presidency, EDA

item.title: [EU Observer] Listen: Europe relaxes methane rules while pledging to cut emissions at COP31
item.description: Negotiators from the European Parliament and the 27 EU member states agreed yesterday to postpone some of the rules aimed at cutting methane emissions. This happened while COP31 was still underway, with the EU pledging to reduce emissions globally. Can the EU be trusted to tackle greenhouse gas emissions?

item.title: [EU Observer] [Interview] Scottish priority is to rejoin the EU after Brexit ‘badly damaged’ UK, Scotland’s Europe minister says
item.description: Scotland, which wants to rejoin the EU and leave the United Kingdom, has pushed for more free movement and less red tape for food and drink exports ahead of a UK-EU summit. Brexit left the UK "badly damaged", Stephen Gethins said.

item.description: EU 'adoption' of the deal's main elements will be delayed until talks on student tuition fees are concluded

item.title: [EU Observer] Chinese diplomacy sets lofty goals for a new era
item.description: China’s ambassador to the EU argues that from climate action to digital security, Beijing’s new diplomatic push seeks to bind Europe and the Global South into a growth model that rejects US-style alliances and old Cold War dividing lines.

item.description: Investors in latest semiconductor financing demand legal protection for coveted collateral

item.title: [DW] The dangers of revising Europe's security architecture
item.description: Experts warn against revising Europe's security framework because they say it would mean granting Moscow its longstanding wish of renegotiating postwar security on the continent.

item.title: [DW] Czechia braces for massive protest against public media reform plans
item.description: A fast-tracked bill to cut public media funding has sparked strikes, rallies and fears for the independence of public broadcasting in Czechia. A massive protest is planned for Prague on Sunday.
